topic: the WWII-era Japanese emperor never personally addressed by the name history calls him, and Japan's pre-1868 habit of renaming eras after disasters
title: The WWII Emperor Who Never Heard His Own Historical Name
description: AI-narrated history commentary. Japan's WWII-era emperor was never personally addressed by the name history now uses for him -- and before 1868, the imperial court didn't just avoid saying his name, it rewrote the calendar itself over bad omens. Original commentary inspired by public trend data, not a reproduction of any single source video.

hook_candidates.text: This WWII emperor never once heard the name history calls him by.
You think 'Emperor Shōwa' was his real title. He never used it himself.
What was Japan's WWII emperor actually called to his own face?
In 1926, a young prince took a name he would never once hear spoken to him.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who's obsessed with WWII documentaries because they want to show them a detail even the History Channel skips.
contradicted_belief: You assume Japan's WWII emperor was addressed by the name history uses for him.
closing_comment: Wild that we call him Emperor Shōwa more than he ever did himself. Know another ruler who never heard their own historical name?

sources.note: Confirms 'Shōwa' was Hirohito's reign-era name, used as his personal historical name only after his 1989 death.
Documents Japan's cultural taboo against naming or discussing the emperor, especially Hirohito.
Confirms era names changed multiple times within a single reign before 1868's one-reign-one-era reform.
